literal: Purity is that which is called desire's absence; and that, truthfulness if desired, will come.
translation: Purity is said to be the absence of desire; and that state will come to those who desire the ultimate truth.
modern: தூய்மை என்பது ஆசைகள் இல்லாமல் இருப்பது ஆகும்; அந்த ஆசையற்ற நிலை மெய்ம்மையை விரும்பினால் உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines true purity not as physical cleanliness, but as the complete absence of desire. It then explains how this state of desirelessness can be achieved: it comes naturally when one desires and seeks the ultimate truth. By shifting one's focus from transient worldly desires to the eternal truth, all other limiting desires fade away. The poet uses phonetic elongation in the words for purity and truth to emphasize their supreme importance.
